24.0.0.en: 1 Wisdom praises herself, and glories among her people. 2 She opens her mouth in the congregation of the Most High, and glories before His hosts, 3 and is exalted among her people, and glorified in the assembly of the saints, 4 and is praised in the multitude of the chosen, and blessed among the blessed, and says: 5 "I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, the firstborn before every creature, 6 and I made the light shine in the heavens forever, and covered all the earth like a mist, 7 and I dwelt in the heights, and set my throne in the pillar of cloud. 8 I alone went round the circle of heaven, and walked in the depth of the deeps, and walked upon the waves of the sea, 9 and my foot trod all the earth, and over every people, 10 and every nation I held sway, 11 and by my power I trod upon the hearts of the great and the small. In all these I sought rest, and in what inheritance should I abide." 12 Then the Creator of all commanded me, and he who possessed me appointed the place of my dwelling, 13 and said: "Dwell in Jacob, and inherit in Israel." 14 Before the age, from the beginning, he possessed me, and to the age I shall not cease, and I ministered before him in the holy tabernacle. 15 And so in Zion I was established, and he gave me a dwelling in the beloved city, and my dominion is in Jerusalem. 16 So I took root in a glorious people, in the portion of the Lord, the portion of His inheritance, and in the assembly of the saints is my abode. 17 I was exalted like the cedar in Lebanon, and like the cypress on the mountains of Hermon. 18 Like the palm tree on the shores, and like rose plants in Jericho. 19 Like the fair olive tree in the plain, and like the plane tree by the water courses in the streets. 20 My fragrance spread like cinnamon and sweet-smelling calamus, and my scent was diffused like choice myrrh. 21 Like galbanum and onycha and stacte, and like the incense of frankincense in the tabernacle. 22 I stretched out my branches like the terebinth, and my branches are branches of glory and grace. 23 I am like the vine that brings forth grace, and my blossoms are fruits of glory and wealth. 24 I am the mother of fair love, and of fear and knowledge and holy hope. 25 In me is all the grace of the way and the truth, and all the hope of life and virtue. 26 Come to me, you who desire me, and be filled with my fruits. 27 For my spirit is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance more delicious than the honeycomb, 28 and my memorial endures to generations of ages. 29 He who eats me will come back to me hungry, and he who drinks me will come back thirsty. 30 He who listens to me will not be put to shame, and he who acts by my guidance will not sin. 31 He who explains me will have eternal life.

24.0.1.en: Wisdom will praise herself, and glory among her people [1].

24.1.0.en: She opens her mouth in the congregation of the Most High, and glories before His might [2].

24.1.1.en: What does the wisdom of God say?

24.1.2.en: a. In calling believers to acquire her, she praises herself and glories among her people, not because she is in need of praise or outward glory, whether from the sons of men or from the heavenly orders, but because she offers what is hers to the believers. As though she were saying to them: What is mine I give to you. For he who finds me bears witness to the glory he receives by being united with me.

24.1.3.en: b. If the heavenly ones glorify me, I desire to lift up my people, in whom I take pride, that they may be joined to the congregation of the Most High, so that their thoughts and their hearts are lifted up to heavenly things.

24.1.4.en: c. If the dwelling of Wisdom is in the heights and her throne is in the pillar of cloud, yet she is not far from all rational creation. For if man has descended to the depths of the abyss (the deeps) because of his disobedience and his deprivation of the source of his life, I am not far wherever I may be found, whether on earth or in the seas or in the abyss; I save him and depart with him to my dwelling in the heights, and join him to the congregation of the Most High. Without partiality I work in the life of the believer, whatever his nationality; I have authority over every people and nation.

24.1.5.en: d. How does Wisdom seek rest? When the beloved rational creature rests in the wisdom of God, she counts every rest of the creature as her own rest, wherever this creature is found.

24.2.0.en: e. Although the wisdom of God fills the whole world, in heaven and on earth, yet she is concerned for the people of God, and so she pitches her tent in Jacob, and her inheritance in Israel [8]. As though the people of God were her house and her inheritance. This is the condition of every true believer, who sings: "I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine" (Song 6:3). The Lord Christ, the wisdom of God and the power of God, assures us: "The kingdom of God is within you" (Lk 17:21).

24.3.0.en: f. The plan of the wisdom of God for our eternal salvation extends to before the creation, and her work continues forever [9].

24.3.1.en: g. The authority of the wisdom of God over all peoples and nations [6], she counts herself working on behalf of him who receives her and responds to her, and she counts him her beloved city and her holy temple, her portion and her inheritance, and she is his portion and his inheritance [10-12]. She asks to settle in the believing person, and that he settle in her.

24.3.2.en: I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth like a mist [3].

24.3.3.en: She refers here to the birth of the Son, begotten of the Father from eternity. St. Ambrose sees that God the Word proceeded from the Father, He who is in the bosom of the Father (Jn 1:18). And that the bosom here means a kind of dwelling wholly deep in the love of the Father and in His nature (not separated from Him), for He dwells in Him always. And He is begotten in His heart, where He uttered the Word, and here He proceeds from the mouth of the Most High, where divine justice (righteousness) proceeds, and from Him wisdom proceeds, and says: "I came forth from the mouth of the Most High" (see Sir 24:3) [1].

24.3.4.en: v It was said that Wisdom came forth from the mouth of the Most High (see Sir 24:3), not outside the Father, but she is with the Father, for "the Word was with God" (Jn 1:1). Not only "with God", but also in God, for He says: "I am in the Father, and the Father in me" (Jn 14:10). And when He comes forth from the Father He does not come forth from a (particular) place, nor is He separated from Him, as one body is separated from another [2].

24.3.5.en: v It does not appear that the Son came forth from any place, but God from God, the Son from the Father, and He has no beginning in the course of time, but came forth from the Father as one begotten, just as the Begotten One Himself said: "I came forth from the mouth of the Most High" (see Sir 24:3) [3].

24.3.6.en: v It is part of the work of His authority that He made us children of God (Jn 1:10 etc.), while the teachings of God reveal to us His begetting with regard to the hypostatic characteristic, for the wisdom of God says: "I came forth from the mouth of the Most High" (see Sir 24:3), meaning not out of compulsion but in complete freedom, not under the bond of authority, but He was begotten with a mysterious begetting, by the hypostatic power of the Supreme Being and the righteousness of authority. Again, of this same Wisdom, who is the Lord Jesus, the Father says elsewhere: "From the womb I begot You before the morning star" (Ps 110:3). He says this not that we should think of a bodily womb, but to show that it is a true begetting, a fitting act [4].

24.3.7.en: St. Ambrose And I pitched my tent in the heights, and my throne is in the pillar of cloud [4].

24.3.8.en: v Solomon (Sirach) shows Him to be the Word of God (who came forth from the mouth of the Most High), by whose hands these works of the world were made. He says: "I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, the firstborn of all creatures. I made in heaven that which shines with a light that does not fade, and like a cloud I covered all the earth; I dwelt in the heights, and my throne is in the pillar of cloud" (see Sir 24:3-5). John says this: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made" (Jn 1:1-3) [5].

24.3.9.en: Fr. Lactantius I alone compassed the circuit of heaven, and walked in the depths of the abyss [5].

24.3.10.en: The one speaking here is the Wisdom of the Eternal One, one with the Father and the Holy Spirit, everlasting; by our union with Him we enjoy immortality. The Apostle Paul said of Him: "The blessed and only Potentate (the One with authority), the King of kings, and Lord of lords; who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto" (1 Tim 6:14-16).

24.3.11.en: St. Augustine distinguishes between the human soul, of which it was said in the creation of Adam: "and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" (Gen 2:7), and the coming forth of the Son or Wisdom from the mouth of God, for it did not say "the mouth of God breathed" but that He came forth from the mouth of God [6].

24.3.12.en: v It cannot be said that Wisdom comes forth from the mouth of the Most High (see Sir 24:5) so as to be outside the Father, but with the Father, because the Word is with God (Jn 1:1), not only with the Father but also in the Father. For He says: "I am in the Father, and the Father in me" (Jn 14:10). But when He came forth from the Father He did not withdraw as from a place, nor was He separated from Him as one body is separated from another. And being in the Father He is not counted as a body in a body [7].

24.3.13.en: St. Ambrose And over the waves of the sea and all the earth, and over every people and every nation I held sway [6].

24.3.14.en: Wisdom works in the life of the universal Church as her one holy people, as she works in the life of the believer as a member of this people. She directs her speech to the holy congregation as to each member of it.

24.3.15.en: In all these I sought a place of rest, and in what inheritance should I take refuge [7].

24.3.16.en: Then the Creator of all commanded me, and He who created me appointed a place for me to live, and said: "Pitch your tent in Jacob, and receive your inheritance in Israel" [8].

24.3.17.en: This passage came to announce the Incarnation of the Son, the wisdom of God, by saying: "appointed a place for me to live", "Pitch your tent in Jacob", "and receive your inheritance in Israel".

24.3.18.en: v Another prophet spoke of the Son in the same way: "This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him" (Bar 3:36). Of whom does he say this? Did he say this of the Father? Of course not! Listen how well he points to the divine plan! For after saying: "This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him", he added: "He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved. Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men" (Bar 3:36-38) [8].

24.3.19.en: v Jeremiah was the first to say that God becomes man, remaining God. This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him [9].

24.3.20.en: St. John Chrysostom Before the ages and from the beginning He created me, and to the age of ages I shall not cease [9].

24.4.0.en: In His holy tent before Him I ministered, and so I was established in Zion [10].

24.5.0.en: And He gave me rest in the beloved city, and my dominion is in Jerusalem [11].

24.6.0.en: So I took root in an honored people, in the portion of the Lord, His inheritance [12].

24.6.1.en: The people were counted glorious because they enjoyed the word of God and His divine promises; so when the believer embraces the word of God in his heart, and enjoys fellowship with Christ, the end of the Law (Rom 10:4), he enjoys the true treasure, for in Him are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge (Col 2:3).

24.7.0.en: Like the cedar tree in Lebanon I rose high, and like the cypress tree on the mountains of Hermon [13].

24.7.1.en: In offering what is hers to the believers, she establishes from them a holy garden that includes six kinds of trees with various flowers and fruits:

24.7.2.en: a. The great cedar of Lebanon (1 Kgs 6:9-11).

24.7.3.en: b. The cypress of the mountains of Hermon (2 Kgs 19:23). c. The palms of En-gedi (2 Chr 28:15).

24.7.4.en: d. The shrubs and roses of Jericho. e. The olive tree (Judg 9:8).

24.7.5.en: f. The plane tree, which rises beside the waters. g. Cinnamon and fragrant calamus (bamboo cane).

24.7.6.en: h. Choice myrrh with a fragrant scent. i. Galbanum (jalina) and onycha and stacte (mastic).

24.8.0.en: j. Frankincense as in the tent of meeting [15].

24.9.0.en: k. Her branches are like the branches of the terebinth, a source of turpentine oil and of tanning materials [16].

24.10.1.en: Like the palm tree in En-gedi I rose, and like rose plants in Jericho, like the fair olive tree in the plain I rose, and like the plane tree beside the waters I rose [14].

24.10.2.en: Like cinnamon and fragrant calamus my fragrance spread, and like choice myrrh my scent was diffused, like galbanum and onycha and stacte, and like the perfume of frankincense in the tent [15].

24.10.3.en: I stretched out my branches like the terebinth, and my branches are glorious branches, full of grace [16].

24.10.4.en: I am like a vine that brings forth grace, and my blossoms bear fruits of glory and wealth [17].

24.10.5.en: I am the mother of pure love and fear, and knowledge, and holy hope.

24.11.0.en: Therefore, being eternal, I am given to all my children who were named through Him (that is, through the Lord) [18].

24.12.0.en: Come to me, you who desire me, and be filled with my fruits [19].

24.12.1.en: She calls her children to come to her with longing, and to be filled with her fruits and her harvest (Prov 9:4-6).

24.13.0.en: For my memorial is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance more delicious than the honeycomb [20].

24.13.1.en: She assures her children that when they draw near to her and enjoy her fruits, they experience her sweetness, which does not leave their memory, and they inherit what is sweeter than honey.

24.14.0.en: Those who eat me will hunger for more, and those who drink me will thirst for more [21].

24.14.1.en: He who eats of her and drinks increases in hunger and thirst for her with great longing. And at the same time he who hungers and thirsts for her enjoys satisfaction by her eternally.

24.14.2.en: v But you will not cease from love, for he whom you see is like one who confuses you, not with any kind of anxiety, but He satisfies you and also does not satisfy you at the same time. When I say that He satisfies you I fear that you will be like one who is full and wishes to depart, as from a meal or a supper. What then shall I say? That He does not satisfy you? Again I fear that it will seem that He does not satisfy you, and that you will seem like one in need, like one who is empty, and this emptiness needs to be filled. So what shall I say but what can be said, though it can hardly be thought? He satisfies you and does not satisfy you also, for I find both in the Holy Bible. While it says: "Blessed are the hungry, for they shall be filled" (Mt 5:6), again it says of Wisdom: "Those who drink thirst again" (see Sir 24:21). No, it did not say: "another time" but "still", because they thirst again, as they were like one who is satisfied once and departs and digests and then returns to drink [10].

24.15.0.en: St. Augustine Those who obey me will not be put to shame, and those who work with me will not sin [22].

24.16.s.en: 2. A practical comment on the speech of Wisdom

24.16.0.en: 32 All these things are the book of life, and the covenant of the Most High and the knowledge of truth. 33 Moses commanded the Law, and the judgments of justice, the inheritance of the house of Jacob and the promises of Israel. 34 The Lord promised David His servant that He would raise up from him the mighty King who sits on the throne of glory forever. 35 He pours out wisdom like Phison, and like the Tigris in the days of the harvests, 36 and fills with understanding like the Euphrates, and like the Jordan in the days of harvest, 37 and makes discipline appear like the light, and like Geon in the days of the vintage. 38 The first did not complete the knowledge of Wisdom, nor will the last search her out, 39 for her thought is wider than the sea, and her counsel deeper than the great deep. 40 I, Wisdom, am the one who makes rivers overflow. 41 I am like a channel from the river, and like a conduit that went out into Paradise. 42 I said, I will water my garden, and irrigate my flower bed; 43 and behold, my channel has become a river, and my river has become a sea. 44 For I shine forth with discipline like the dawn and make it known to the ends of the earth. 45 I penetrate all the depths of the earth and look upon all who sleep, and I enlighten all who hope in the Lord. 46 I pour out teaching like prophecy, and leave it behind for the generations of ages. 47 See that my toil was not for myself alone, but also for all who seek wisdom.

24.16.1.en: All these things are the book of the covenant with the Most High God and the Law which Moses commanded us, an inheritance for the congregations of Jacob [23].

24.16.2.en: Wisdom binds them to the covenant with God and to keeping the Law as an inheritance for them [23].

24.16.3.en: Do not hesitate that you are strong in the Lord; cleave to Him, and He will establish you, for the Lord Almighty is God alone. And beside Him there is no other savior. [24]

24.16.4.en: This chapter is regarded as the center of the book. It rains surpassing blessings upon the souls of believers who seek wisdom. And lest anyone think that what Wisdom says does not concern him, because he is too weak to enjoy her, she encourages him, saying: "Do not hesitate that you are strong in the Lord; cleave to Him, and He will establish you" [24]. For He alone is the mighty Savior. Man himself cannot save himself, nor can his brothers save him.

24.16.5.en: v "He cannot give to God an atonement for himself, or the price of the ransom of his soul (even if he toiled forever)" (Ps 48:7-8) LXX. So do not ask your brother for a ransom for you, but ask Him who surpasses your nature, for He is not a mere man, but God incarnate, Jesus Christ; who alone is able to offer a ransom to God (the Father) for us all. For God set Him forth as a propitiation through faith in His blood (Rom 3:25). Moses was a brother to Israel, and was not able to save him. Now can any ordinary man save? Therefore the passage declares: "No brother can save?" and another passage asks in earnest: "Shall man be saved?" (Ps 48:7) LXX.

24.16.6.en: Moses did not free his people from sin, but asked God for exemption from the punishment for sin. At any rate, he was not able to ransom himself when he sinned. For after he had wrought many great wonders and signs that he had seen, he uttered these words that express doubt: "Hear now, ye rebellious doubters: must we fetch you water out of this rock?" (see Num 20:10). For this reason, because of these words the Lord said to Moses and Aaron: "Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them" (Num 20:12), and so he did not offer a ransom to God for himself.

24.16.7.en: In truth, what great thing can a man find sufficient to offer as a ransom for himself? But one thing was found worthy to be offered for all people together. This was offered as the price for the redemption of our souls: the blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, holy and most honored, which He shed for all of us; therefore we were bought with a great price (1 Pet 2:22).

24.16.8.en: If the brother does not save, can a man be saved? But if the brother cannot save us, then He who saved us is not a man. Therefore do not think, because He dwelt among us "in the likeness of our sinful flesh" (Rom 8:3), that our Lord is a mere man, being unable to perceive the power of His divinity, He who has no need to offer a ransom for Himself, nor to redeem Himself, for "he did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth" (1 Pet 2:22). No one has sufficiency to save himself, unless He come who removes the captivity of men not by ransoms nor by gifts, as it is written in Isaiah (52:3), but by His blood.

24.16.9.en: And although we are not His brothers, since we became enemies by our disobedience, He who is not a mere man but God, after the freedom He gave us, called us His brothers. He says: "I will declare thy name unto my brethren" (Ps 22:22; Heb 2:12). He who saves us, if you examine His nature, is neither a brother nor a man, but if you examine His condescension to us by grace, He calls us His brothers; He comes down to our human nature, He who does not give God a ransom for Himself, but for the whole world.

24.16.10.en: He has no need of a ransom; He Himself is the propitiation. "For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens; who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's" (Heb 7:26-27). Then he says: "And he worked (even if he toiled) forever or lived to the end" (see Ps 49:8-9). For the existence of (the Redeemer) Himself, and His power, and His persevering nature work with toil in this life, and when He was weary from the journey He sat at the well (Jn 4:5) [11].

24.16.11.en: St. Basil the Great v When I call all these things to my memory (if I speak according to feelings), I am struck with a kind of dreadful fear and cold terror, lest through distraction of thought and preoccupation with vanities I fall from the love of God and become an object of insult to Christ. For he who now deceives us and strives by every means to urge us to ignore our Benefactor through the confusion of the enticements of the world that leap upon us and trample on us to destroy our souls, then, in the presence of the Lord, rebukes us for our impudence, and gloats over our disobedience and apostasy. He who never created us nor died for us counts us among his followers in disobedience and neglect of the commandments of God.

24.16.12.en: This insult directed to the Lord, and this victory for our enemy, seems to me more terrible than the punishments of Gehenna, because we give the enemy of Christ material for boasting, and an argument to exalt himself over Him who died for us and rose again. For this reason we are debtors to Him in a very special sense, as it is written (Rom 8:12). Therefore it befits us all the more to observe the love of God.

24.16.13.en: My aim, as I said before, is not to present the whole subject, for that is impossible, but to implant in your souls in brief the remembrance of keeping the divine longing awake within you [12].

24.16.14.en: St. Basil the Great v Question: What if someone was commanded and refused the commandment, but afterward of his own will left off this refusal and fulfilled the commandment? (Mt 21:29).

24.16.15.en: Answer: By his refusal he is considered an opponent (of the commandment), and one who provokes others to practice similar evils. Let him realize that he is subject to this sentence: "The rebel stirs up every evil, so the Lord sends a cruel messenger against him" (see Prov 17:11). Therefore let him be convinced that he is not resisting or obeying a man, but the Lord who says: "He that heareth you heareth me; and he that despiseth you despiseth me" (Lk 10:16).

24.16.16.en: But by remembering the commandment he has shown repentance; let him apologize first, and then, if it is permitted him, fulfill the work [13].

24.16.17.en: St. Basil the Great This Law fills people with wisdom, like Phison and the Tigris[14] in the days of the firstfruits [25].

24.16.18.en: Ben Sira used what is mentioned in the Old Testament about the rivers, especially in the garden of Eden, for he sees in them the overflowing through the enjoyment of the characteristics of wisdom (Gen 2:10-14).

24.16.19.en: He speaks of the small channel that was turned into a great river, through his practical experience, where he looks at what he acquired of wisdom at the beginning of his life, and as he was asking God continually to give him wisdom, the channel of wisdom within him turned into a river that overflows upon many. He offers them the waters of life, than which no river overflows with the like, therefore he presented to them six famous rivers. Four of them are mentioned in the story of creation (Gen 2:10-14) watering the garden of Eden, and the Nile and the Jordan [25-28].

24.16.20.en: If her waters are better than all the rivers, they are very wide, so that the river becomes a sea, and at the same time, in a spirit of humility, she becomes like a channel from the river or a conduit that waters the garden. She cares for the believer to water him with a channel or small conduit, and when she enters his depths the channel becomes a river, and the river becomes a sea. What are these waters that overflow upon the human soul as from a channel but the divine wisdom that offers a life full of blessings (Isa 58:11; Ezek 47:1-12).

24.16.21.en: The waters of wisdom are also a light that shines in the soul like the dawn that gleams from afar.

24.16.22.en: He did not say like the river Jordan, as he mentioned rivers found in the lands of the Gentiles, for Ben Sira often declared what the Gentiles enjoy through the preaching of the Gospel.

24.16.23.en: v "Hear this, all you peoples; give ear, all you inhabitants of the world. O you earthborn, and you sons of men, rich and poor alike" (Ps 49:1-2).

24.16.24.en: The place of assembly is enormous, where the psalm calls all the nations to listen, and all who fill the world with their dwellings. I think that by this exalted proclamation he draws not only the earthborn but all the sons of men, rich and poor, and calls them to listen.

24.16.25.en: What kind of watchtower is this, standing in its height over all the earth to see all the nations from afar, and embracing the whole world with its eyes? What kind of herald is so loud of voice that he cries out and many ears hear him at the same time? What place is able to contain such gatherings? What greatness and what wisdom has this Teacher, to give instructions fitting for this great assembly? Wait a little, and you will learn that what follows is fitting to the promise (made to them). For He who gathers all, and calls them to the proclamation, is the Paraclete, the Spirit of truth, who gathers together the prophets and the apostles who are saved. Of whom it was said: "Their sayings have reached all the earth, and their words the ends of the world" (Ps 19:5) LXX. Therefore the Church was gathered from all classes of people (of life), so that no one may be left without help from her.

24.16.26.en: There are three groups called, which embrace the whole human race: Gentiles, and inhabitants of the world who are earthborn, and the sons of men, rich and poor. Who then was left and not called to listen? Those who are outside the faith are called by the call of the Gentiles. The inhabitants of the world are those who are in the Church.

24.16.27.en: The earthborn, who are wise in the affairs of earthly things and cling to the pleasures of the flesh.

24.16.28.en: The sons of men are those who walk with some seriousness and train their minds, for prudence is the mark of man.

24.16.29.en: The rich and the poor have their identity known from them: the former have increasing possessions of the necessities of life, and the latter stand in need of them.

24.16.30.en: And since the Physician of souls did not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance (Mt 9:13), in His call He placed first in each group those who are condemned. The Gentiles are worse than the inhabitants of the world, and yet they were chosen first in the call, so that the sick may come first, to enjoy the care of the Physician. And after that the earthborn were placed before the sons of men, and the rich before the poor.

24.16.31.en: The group that was hopeless and whose salvation was harder was called before the poor. Such is the tenderness of the Physician, offering His help first to those who are weakest.

24.16.32.en: At the same time, sharing in the summons is union in peace, so that those who until that time were opposing one another, because of differences of customs, by assembling together, grow accustomed to one another in love. Let the rich man know that he is called by the same proclamation as the poor man. It says: "rich and poor alike" (Ps 49:2).

24.16.33.en: Let arrogance toward those who are in greater need, and the haughtiness of wealth, be left outside; with this enter the Church of God. So let not the rich treat the poor with disdain, nor the poor shrink trembling under the authority of the wealthy. Let not the sons of men despise the earthborn, nor the earthborn isolate themselves from them. Let the Gentiles grow accustomed to dealing with the inhabitants of the world, and the inhabitants of the world through love receive them as friends and guests through the covenants [15].

24.16.34.en: St. Basil the Great And she fills them with understanding, like the Euphrates and like the Jordan in the days of harvest [26].

24.16.35.en: This Law shines forth with teaching like the light, and it overflows with teaching like the Nile, like Geon in the days of the (grape) vintage [27].

24.16.36.en: In speaking of the Law that shines forth with teaching, he does not liken it only to the rivers that watered the garden of Eden, but added to them other rivers such as the Nile, because the divine Law is not limited to the Jews alone. Our Christ overflows upon us with grace, and as the Apostle says: "In whom we have redemption through his blood... according to the riches of his grace; wherein he hath abounded toward us in all wisdom and prudence" (Eph 1:7-8).

24.16.37.en: v "The stream of the river maketh glad the city of God" (Ps 46:4). The waters of the sea stirred up by the winds swell and rise, but the stream of the river flows without disturbance. It flows quietly, for those who have been counted worthy to receive it. Therefore it makes glad the city of God, and now the righteous man drinks of the living waters (Jn 4:10), but in the future he will drink abundantly when his name is written among those who dwell in the city of God.

24.16.38.en: Now he drinks as in a mirror, darkly (1 Cor 13:12), for what he takes of divine contemplations is little, but then he will be filled, and his river will be able to overflow with joy in the city of God.

24.16.39.en: What then is the river of God? It is the Holy Spirit who flows in those who are worthy, who truly have faith in Christ. "He that believeth on me, as he says, out of his belly shall flow rivers..." (Jn 7:38); also he who drinks of the water that I give him, it shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life (Jn 4:13). This is the river that makes glad the city of God. It is the stream of the Holy Spirit [16].

24.16.40.en: St. Basil the Great Just as the first man did not know Wisdom completely, so the last man does not search out her depths [28].

24.16.41.en: With the understanding and wisdom with which the first man was endowed, he could not reach the depths of divine wisdom, and humanity remains unable to do so, even the last man. Ben Sira affirms that there is not one person throughout all ages and to the end of the age who is able to comprehend the depths of the wisdom of God.

24.16.42.en: For her thought is deeper than the sea, and her counsel deeper than the great abyss [29].

24.16.43.en: Fr. Caesarius, Bishop of Arles, sees that the believer, as he eats and drinks the word of God, enters into a dialogue with God, and this dialogue does not cease, therefore Satan cannot overcome him [17].

24.16.44.en: And I am like a channel from the river, and like a conduit that went out into a garden [30].

24.16.45.en: I said: "I will water my garden, and drench the beds of my well-arranged flowers."

24.16.46.en: And behold, my channel has become a river, and my river has become a sea [31].

24.16.47.en: What is this channel that became a sea? St. Basil the Great sees that it is the tears of repentance.

24.16.48.en: v Who prays with streams of tears receives storms of rain at the right time? Who washes away sins, imitating the blessed David, who poured out tears upon his bed? Who washed the feet of strangers and rinsed off the dust of travel, so that even in time of need this person intercedes with God, asking that the drought cease? Who supports a child deprived of parents, that in return God may supply him with wheat, as an orphan shattered by contrary winds? Who cares for a widow struck by the hardships of life, so that the help we need may return to us? Tear up unjust contracts, so that sins also may be loosed.

24.16.49.en: Remove debts with exorbitant interest, so that the earth may bring forth its ordinary fruits [18].

24.16.50.en: St. Basil the Great I make discipline shine like the morning, and I make it shine afar [32].

24.17.0.en: I pour out teaching like prophecy, and leave it behind me for the generations to come [33].

24.17.1.en: v "You shall enter into the generation of your fathers" [19]. I think he is speaking of the sinner who knows God according to what his fathers handed down to him, but has not acquired anything additional by his own thought, nor added to his knowledge of the truth by himself.

24.17.2.en: He says: "O Lord, You are near", and at the same time he has a great idea of You as existing in the generations of his fathers. While he walks in laziness, and his spirit is occupied with earthly and fleshly things, which stagger in riches and luxury, and his mind is loaded with the cares of life, therefore "he does not see the light" [see 19].

24.17.3.en: As they entrust their leadership to blind teachers, they deprive themselves of the blessing of the light. This saying, "He enters into the generation of his fathers", carries the same meaning. This is said of those who pass through an evil life, and of teachings issuing from their fathers, but who are estranged from godliness; not only will it punish them, but it drives out those who lay down corrupt teachings. This is what he means by saying: "He enters into the generation of his fathers". Not only he who has blameworthy thoughts about God, but also he who leads others to this destruction. So are those who receive this evil from their forefathers, which is strengthened through persevering in it by habits for a long time, and there is difficulty in cleansing it. "He does not see the light", for they are sent into the outer darkness, where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth (Mt 8:12). This comes upon them according to the just judgment of God, since they hated the light in this life, because they did evil.

24.17.4.en: "Man being in honor did not understand; he is compared to the senseless beasts, and is like them." What a hateful report! Man? This one whom You made a little lower than the angels" (Heb 2:7), and of whom Solomon says: "Man is a great thing; the man who is pitied is honored" (Prov 20:6) LXX. He is compared to the senseless beasts, and becomes like them", because he does not realize his honor, and bows down to the desires of the flesh [19].

24.18.0.en: St. Basil the Great And as you see, I did not strive for myself alone, but for all who seek wisdom [34].

24.19.s.en: That I may know You, and love You and possess You!

24.19.0.en: v Do You need to glory, O Wisdom of God, You who fill the heavens and the earth?

24.19.1.en: You glory in Your wondrous love for us sinners, that we may come to know You, and cleave to You and love You.

24.19.2.en: You went forth with Your Cross to shake the foundations of the abyss, and carry us to Your Paradise, and count us as the congregation of the Most High, and offer us the impossible!

24.19.3.en: v You came forth from the mouth of the Father, without being separated from Him.

24.19.4.en: And You gave us the Spirit of adoption, so that we have boldness to speak with You.

24.19.5.en: You came into the circle of heaven, and You are its Creator.

24.19.6.en: By Your Spirit You lift us from glory to glory, until we meet You face to face.

24.19.7.en: v It is wondrous that in Your humility and love You seek rest in us, and ask for an inheritance for Yourself!

24.19.8.en: Your rest is to establish from our weakness a new heaven, and so rest within us!

24.19.9.en: And Your inheritance is to turn our hearts into Your divine Kingdom!

24.19.10.en: v You pitched Your tent in Jacob, and counted Israel an inheritance for Yourself, and here You offer me Your Kingdom within me, that I may sing: "The Lord is my portion, saith my soul!"

24.19.11.en: Your Kingdom in my heart has no likeness on earth.

24.19.12.en: With what shall I describe it? Is it a unique garden?

24.19.13.en: Whenever I stretch out my hands to take of its fruits, my hunger for it increases, and whenever I drink of its waters, my thirst for it increases.

24.19.14.en: v The more I cleave to You, the more I feel that I am strong.

24.19.15.en: I sing with the Apostle: "I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me" (Phil 4:13).

24.19.16.en: You alone are the Lord Almighty; I have no savior but You!

24.19.17.en: What price is greater than Your precious blood, shed as a ransom for me?

24.19.18.en: What heavenly creature or what prophet among the prophets atones for my sins but You?

24.19.19.en: v Truly You are the lover of all mankind, offering Your Law and Your covenant not to a particular people, but to all humanity.

24.19.20.en: In Your infancy Judaism was stirred up against You, even those who knew the prophecies concerning You.

24.19.21.en: And the Magi came to You from the East to worship You.

24.19.22.en: You fled in Your infancy to Egypt, to establish Your Church there.

24.19.23.en: The world feels Your love and is indebted to You for its salvation.

24.19.24.en: v Your care for humanity is surpassing; Your grace waters my garden, and the fragrance of its beautiful flowers rises, the heavenly ones smell it and rejoice at Your wondrous work in us.

24.19.25.en: The channel of Your love overflows with grace to water my depths.

24.19.26.en: And as the garden widens and grows, Your channel turns into a great river.

24.19.27.en: And my garden remains thirsty for You more and more, and Your great river turns into a great sea.

24.19.28.en: And with every growth in understanding and knowledge, I realize that I am still on the shore of the sea of Your wisdom.

24.19.29.en: Would that all humanity shared with me my experience of Your grace and love and care!
